mechanism_narrative: A low federal funds rate indicates an accommodative monetary policy, which may stimulate economic growth and lead to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 40% of the 20-day periods following low FEDFUNDS.

mechanism_narrative: A high unemployment rate suggests economic weakness, which may lead to negative S&P 500 returns as consumer spending and business investment could decline.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive returns in more than 50% of the 20-day periods when UNRATE exceeds 6%.

mechanism_narrative: Increasing retail sales indicate strong consumer demand, which may boost corporate earnings and lead to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 30% of the 60-day periods following RSAFS growth.

mechanism_narrative: A slowdown in industrial production may signal weaker economic conditions, leading to negative S&P 500 returns as corporate earnings could be affected.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive returns in more than 60% of the 20-day periods when INDPRO growth is below 0.5%.

mechanism_narrative: When employment increases but unemployment also rises, it may indicate inefficiencies in the labor market, leading to negative S&P 500 returns as businesses may face higher costs.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive returns in more than 40% of the 20-day periods when both PAYEMS increases and UNRATE rises.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in housing starts indicates a strong housing market, which may lead to positive S&P 500 returns as related industries benefit from increased activity.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 30% of the 60-day periods when HOUST exceeds 1.1 million units.

mechanism_narrative: A slowdown in GDP growth may indicate a recession, leading to negative S&P 500 returns as economic activity and corporate earnings decline.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive returns in more than 50% of the 60-day periods when GDPC1 growth is below 2%.

mechanism_narrative: High inflation may lead to tighter monetary policy, increasing borrowing costs and leading to negative S&P 500 returns as companies face reduced margins and consumer spending slows.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive returns in more than 40% of the 20-day periods when CPIAUCSL exceeds 240.
